system.summary: Homophonic pigpen: cell shape (with optional inner stroke) plus 1-3 dots; common letters have several signs.
system.notes: Shapes A-I = the nine pigpen cells (A=RB, B=LRB, C=LB, D=TRB, E=box, F=TLB, G=TR, H=TLR, I=TL in archive orientation), K = stem with a middle bar, X = rare extra sign; * = inner stroke; digit = dot count. Two signs are polyphones resolved by context: C1 = f/q, F2 = l/h. Special signs: '@' (circle/9) and a numeral-like sign, plus the number 67 written in clear in the cipher on f. 241.

prior_solution.where: Sheila Richards, Secret Writings (1973), as reported by G. Lasry (email 25 Sept 2026); the book was not seen here and a web search found no bibliographic record.

solution.what: Pencil flap key and all grid orientations/dot orders tested
Full hand transcription of p. 3 (hand_p3.txt)
Homophonic annealing (hc3.py) lands on French; anchors fixed by hand
f. 243 read almost in full, f. 241 in fragments

Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): the letter was decoded by Sheila Richards in Secret Writings (1973). Not found by the Sept 2026 web search; not seen, not used. Independent re-solution, dropped from the ciphertext-only list for Klaus Schmeh.
f. 241 hand-transcribed column by column from deskewed 5x crops of the DECODE image (hand_p1.txt, 20 columns, ~414 signs); auto-segmentation (v1_glyphs2.json) used only to locate columns

f. 241 decoded with key.json unchanged: it is the closing page (vostre tres humble et fidel serviteur ..., De Nancy le .. decembre); 'sa Majesté' after a long illness, an envoy, 'vous conjurant me faire faveur d'asseurer Sa Majesté du zele...'
New values from f. 241: H3 = z (zele), C*2 = q (ce qui); C1 confirmed as polyphone f/q (faveur, confiance vs que, qu'il)

f. 242 hand-transcribed (hand_p2.txt); found to be a second copy of f. 243 with the same line breaks and the same signs (cj, cp, cs read independently agree sign for sign); top of six columns hidden by the paper flap

F2 = l/h polyphone, prompted by f. 241 c0 'etclerisce' after f. 243's last word 'honnor-': gives 'honnore et cheris ce qui', and on f. 243 'gentilhomme', 'choses', 'homme', 'l'honeur' without breaking 'plus sensible'
Page order fixed: f. 243 -> f. 241 (f. 243 ends 'je vous honnor-', f. 241 begins '-e et cheris ce qui se peut'); f. 242 is a duplicate of f. 243

measure.py on reading.txt: signs read as sense f. 241 86.5%, f. 243 81.7%, letter (ff. 243+241) 728/867 = 84.0%; duplicate f. 242 73.5% of visible signs. lm.best_language: fr-1600-letters first (-2.1/char) on both pages
Low-resolution reading of corner shapes on f. 242 cq/cr/cn confused open sides (C/F/I, B/D); independent reading abandoned there and the f. 243 signs adopted after collation

Neighbouring DECODE records opened: R922 (NAH), R923, R924, R925, R928, R929 (SP 106/10 ff. 233-240, 245-247: digit codes, Henrietta Maria 1645-46 group), R930 (f. 249, strip of alchemical-type symbols), R931/R932 (f. 251-252 numeric), R933 (a key sheet); R926 and ff. 237, 244 have no record. No other pigpen letter, no decipherment or clear copy of R927

Web search (SP 106/10 pigpen, Nancy), Lasry GL.htm copies in the repo, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana index (only the Walsingham-Wilkes pigpen): no edition or calendar entry; CSP not searchable without a year or names
Image routes checked: TNA Discovery has no digitised images of SP 106/10; DECODE serves only the 2300-px PNGs already used (no larger original on the record)

Every sign of the unread words on ff. 243 and 241 re-read from 3-4x tiles of each glyph (auto-segmentation boxes used only as locators): 15 columns of f. 243 and 6 of f. 241 corrected (open sides of corner shapes, dot counts, inner strokes, missed and cancelled signs)

New readings: 'je ne pouvois', 'ayant appris', 'lequel salua dernierement', 'mon maistre', 'vous aviés creu quelques choses au prejudice', 's'il fut esté personne en qui je peusse prendre confiance, vous eussiés congnu par luy que je ne cheris rien tant que les occasions de vous en tesmoigner des effets', 'l'honneur de vostre bienveuillance'; f. 241 'ledit', 'de la part de Sa Majesté', 'je leur ouvriray mon coeur', 'faveur d'asseurer'
F*1 = l (not t): 'que les occasions' twice; D*1 = o (pouvois)

Joint hill-climb of all sign values over the three pages with fr-1600-letters (anneal.py): score -2.106 -> -2.002/char, but it turns B2 g->s (gentilhomme, longue, tesmoigner) and K2 h->d (humble, honnor); LM-only over-fitting on 1300 signs. Only F*1 = l kept
measure.py: letter 843/882 = 95.6% read as sense (97.1% excluding 14 code/name signs); f. 243 98.3%, f. 241 92.5%. Before: 84.0%

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 843 tokens, 35 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.007 per letter; random keys -5.815 (z 5.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.967 (mean -3.009, z 30.4); annealer on the real text -2.032. Verdict: pass.

Outside contribution reviewed (WAINUT, PR #30; done separately with Claude Opus 5.5 subagents, not counted as this project's work): their independent key and transcription agree on all 20 shared signs, 95.4% same dot count over 849 aligned signs. Their claim that images P2 and P3 are one leaf (flap down / lifted) checked on the DECODE images and confirmed, so f. 242 is not a second copy and the P2/P3 agreement checked the transcription only. Adopted 'voiage' (f. 243 c2), 'sieur' (f. 241 c17) and the split of code signs into [67], [6], [@]; c12 'service du [67] et du vostre' kept as a conjecture; signature Nicle/Ville open; persons (Henri de Livron, marquis de Ville; Charles IV; Charles I; Earl of Holland; Dec 1629) recorded as a hypothesis, CSP Venice XXI note checked online

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.901; polyphony 0.015; 39 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.032

outcome.method_basis: The homophonic pigpen key was built by annealing (hc3.py) on a hand transcription of f. 243 until French emerged, then fixed with guessed anchors ('monsieur', 'vous supplie'); the pencil key on the flap was tested and rejected, and no prior solution was found at the time; Lasry later reported it decoded by Sheila Richards in Secret Writings (1973), so this is an independent re-solution.
outcome.notes: All three pages transcribed. The letter runs f. 243 -> f. 241; f. 242 (image P2) is the same leaf as f. 243 with the flap down, not a copy (corrected 12 Oct 2026 after WAINUT, PR #30). Written at Nancy in December by a client ('vostre tres humble et fidel serviteur', signature read 'Nicle') to a 'Monsieur'; it concerns the journey ('voiage', WAINUT reading) of 'ce gentilhomme', an envoy to congratulate 'Sa Majesté' on recovering from a long illness, and assurances of zeal for the King's service. Classed read on 3 Oct 2026 (write-up update): the letter is 95.6% read as sense and every open piece is blocked from outside (blots and a stain on f. 241, no second copy or better image; name signs with no key; f. 243 read at 98.3%).
